task: Write a Gate 1 test: run the live baseline and window-16 candidates on the unseen 2018-2024 store.
steps: Read GO_LIVE.md for the Gate 1 criteria
Reused position_size_test.exit_of/simulate and gemma_graded.gates_for instead of new simulators
Wrote candidate rules into the docstring before running
Sanity-ran on the 2y store: account -11.1% vs documented -11.6% -- matches
Committed BEFORE running on the 2018 store, so the rules provably came first
why: A rule found on 2024-26 must hold on data it was not found on. Committing first proves no threshold was tuned to the result.
lesson: Check a new backtest reproduces a known number before trusting it on new data. The documented -0.024R was ungated and pre-cost; gated with costs is -0.059R -- different populations, not a bug.

task: Make mpc_test.py run on any store with an end date.
steps: Store was a module global; on Windows, spawned workers re-import the module and never see a changed global
Passed store in each job tuple instead
Added --store, --until, --range, --workers and a per-period account view reusing gate1_test.account
Left every MPC rule unchanged
why: Candidate 5 needs the unseen store; the test's rules were fixed earlier and must not move.
lesson: On Windows ProcessPoolExecutor, pass configuration through job arguments, not globals.

task: Fix a SyntaxError in mpc_test.py introduced by a scripted edit.
steps: Background run exited with 'unterminated f-string literal'

A Python-in-heredoc replacement turned the escape 
 into a real newline inside an f-string
Restored the escape; ran py_compile on every touched script before running anything
why: A crashed background job wastes the run slot and can be missed.
lesson: After any scripted edit, run `python -m py_compile <files>` before launching long jobs. Read the job's output, not just its exit notice.

task: Pair the operator's pasted Alpaca fills into trades and find what the winners share.
steps: Grouped partial fills by symbol and date, summed buys and sells -> dollar P&L per trade
Filled the three trades whose buys were off the page from data/broker_archive/*__orders.json
Checked one hypothesis (daily ATR) against the live trades with gate1_test._atr_pct -- no difference
Noticed wins clustered in a broad market (Aug) and losses in a narrow one (late Sep), consistent with Gate 1's 2021
why: Fourteen trades cannot prove a pattern; they can suggest one to test on thousands of setups.
lesson: Live trades generate hypotheses; the backtest decides. Say plainly how small the sample is.

task: Pre-register and test a market-breadth filter.
steps: Added load_trades() with a pickle cache so new tests reuse the 30-minute scan
Wrote the rule (>= 6 of 11 sectors with positive median 1-month return) and DISCLOSED that it was inspired by results already seen
Committed before running
2y store: +0.033R kept vs -0.157R skipped, p=0.058
why: A filter inspired by data must be tested where it could fail, with the contamination stated.
lesson: When an idea comes from data you have already looked at, say so in the docstring and design the check (per-period split) around it.

task: Explain why the Gate 1 account was +35.9% while the average trade lost.
steps: Noticed mean % per trade -0.186% cannot compound to +35.9% at a fixed 20% position
Replicated position_size_test.simulate and recorded which setups it took and skipped
Taken +0.078R vs skipped -0.354R on 2018; on the 2y store -0.047R vs -0.087R
Concluded slot luck, not edge, because it does not repeat
why: A headline number that contradicts its own parts is a bug or a selection effect; either way it must be explained before anyone relies on it.
lesson: When totals and averages disagree, rebuild the total from its parts and find which subset carries it.

task: Record Gate 1 results in WORKLIST.md and GO_LIVE.md.
steps: New section §30 placed above §29 (newest first)
Nulls recorded as plainly as hits, with the 2y vs unseen comparison
Corrected a stale number and fingerprint in GO_LIVE with change-log rows instead of silent edits
MISTAKE: proposed a breadth filter without first reading WORKLIST §25, which had already found breadth null
why: The operator decides funding from these docs; they must match the evidence.
lesson: Before proposing any filter, grep WORKLIST.md for it -- most ideas have already been tried. GO_LIVE.md changes go in its change log, never silently.

task: Test closer take-profits and 3-4 rung ladders the operator proposed.
steps: Grepped WORKLIST first: §24 (close natural targets worst) and §27 (quick 1.5R cap worse) already pointed against
Fixed arms in the docstring, committed, then ran
Checked the new walker reproduces the live baseline (-0.059R) before trusting other arms
Skipped the 30-minute 2018 run for ladders that already lost to the baseline on the 2y store
why: The operator asked; prior evidence did not cover targets under 1.5R.
lesson: A fixed-stop ladder equals the average of its single-target arms -- reason it out before running. Raising win rate by shrinking wins does not change expectancy when losers stay at -1R.

task: Explain why today's orders were cancelled.
steps: GET /v2/orders (read-only) since 10-04, nested legs; times are UTC, AK = UTC-8
Matched each to audit rows and logs/scheduled.log
Pulled 15m SIP bars to see whether SLB's limit was ever touched (missed by 4-5 cents, then +1.5%)
Found protect.py leaves a breached position naked for a human -- frozen path, flagged not changed
why: Cancelled orders hide execution bugs; each needs a cause.
lesson: Never change the frozen trading path to fix a gap mid-window; report it with the trade-off and let the operator choose.

task: Let the operator scan a pasted list of non-S&P names without trading them.
steps: Read trade.py to copy its exact fetch -> drop_incomplete -> scan -> fresh/live/session checks
Wrote a separate read-only script instead of widening the live universe (that would end window 15)
Dropped IBIT/MSTR/COIN from the list per the stocks-only rule and said so in the file
Checked its day % against the operator paste before trusting it
why: The operator wants to see more names; the frozen path must not change mid-window.
lesson: When asked to extend the live system, first offer a view-only tool that reuses the live functions; it answers the question without touching the frozen path.

task: Test the momentum engine on stocks it was never tested on (S&P 400 + 600).
steps: Read momentum_factor.py, backtest.engine.run and index_history to reuse the exact S&P 500 machinery
Kept every rule identical to the S&P 500 run (top 10, 63d/21d, 10y) -- a new universe is the test, not new settings
Wrote PASS / STRONG PASS / FAIL in the docstring before running
Checked the benchmark symbols (^SP400, ^SP600) exist before committing
Used a 5-seed random control so the comparison is pattern vs identical machinery
why: The 10y S&P 500 result has been seen; only new names can confirm it.
lesson: Out-of-sample can mean other stocks, not only other years. Keep the rules frozen when changing the universe.

steps: Run printed 0 priced and crashed on an empty list
Fetched AAPL with range max/20y/30y: max returns 169 QUARTERLY bars, 30y returns daily from 1996
Switched to 30y; data-request fix only, rules unchanged, so committing after the rule commit is fine
why: A test that silently gets the wrong bar size measures nothing.
lesson: Yahoo range=max downsamples to quarterly. Print bar counts and first dates for one symbol before a long multi-symbol run.

task: Test published momentum crash guards on two datasets with a pre-set pass rule.
steps: Audited MidCap 400 membership drift first: log starts 2012, so the 2000-15 test could only use the S&P 500
Applied each guard to the random control too, so cash time cannot pass for skill
Committed arms and the three-part pass rule before running
Trend filter missed the t bar by 0.01: recorded as FAIL, not rounded up
why: Momentum crashed 62% in 2000-15; funding needs a guard proven on data it was not tuned on.
lesson: A near miss on a pre-set bar is a miss. Report how close it came, and move to new (forward) data instead of moving the bar.

task: Start a trial ledger and find historical earnings data for a post-earnings drift test.
steps: Counted every test run (26 today + ~35 earlier) so new results are judged against the size of the search
Probed the Nasdaq earnings API on 5 past dates before writing a collector: EPS, forecast and surprise go back to 2010
Dropped marketCap from the collector: Nasdaq returns today's value on past rows (lookahead)
Wrote and committed the PEAD rules while the data was still downloading -- the cleanest possible pre-registration
why: The operator wants a real edge to fund; only published effects tested with rules fixed in advance can be trusted after ~60 tries.
lesson: Probe a data source on a few samples before building on it, and check every field for lookahead (here: market cap). Write the test before the data arrives when you can.

task: Build the momentum engine as a dry run.
steps: Wrote 18 tests first; ran them red (module missing)
Implemented small pure modules: signal (rank, trend), book (tranches, rebuild, orders), state (atomic JSON)
One test failed because the TEST passed 210 closes where the rule needs more than 210 -- fixed the test after confirming the backtest uses the same rule
Kept the script dry-run only: no broker call in the file at all
Ran --preview before recording; it surfaced whole-share underweighting and 8/10 one-sector concentration
Full suite green (1030) before committing
why: Goal 1: run own money like a fund. Build exactly what was measured; log untested ideas instead of enforcing them.
lesson: When a new test fails, check whether the test or the code disagrees with the measured rule before changing either. Previews catch real-world problems (share rounding, concentration) that unit tests do not.

task: Audit the TradingAgents integration and fix what was wrong.
steps: Checked task status, worker config, data vendors, per-run logs, retention and the scorecard
Found every decision agent falling back to free text; probed three structured-output methods in the TradingAgents venv on a toy schema before changing anything
Patched the method in our worker (beside _thinking_off), not in TradingAgents' install, so an upgrade cannot silently undo it
Verified with one full real pass: no fallbacks, same rating, faster
why: A record-only layer still has to record the right thing; regex-parsed prose can silently mislabel ratings.
lesson: Read the worker's own log, not just its exit code -- 0 failed runs hid three fallbacks per run. Probe a fix in isolation, then confirm on one real run.

task: Build a monthly momentum report with TradingAgents on each pick, record-only.
steps: Reused tradingagents_pass._run_one so the report inherits scan-deadline protection
Stored reports under data/momentum, outside the 30-day advisor cleanup, because the later test needs the reasoning
Refused market hours unless --force (the scanner owns the GPU)
Fixed the #44 rule for when a rating may become a filter BEFORE collecting any ratings
why: The operator wants TradingAgents tied into live trading; the honest route is to record first under a pre-set rule and promote only on evidence.
lesson: When asked to wire a model into decisions, wire it into the record first and write down now what result would earn it the decision.

task: Monitor v2: give Gemma the trade math as codes, deterministic settings, record-only; daily momentum watch.
steps: Pre-registered #45 BEFORE the first live review
Kept the audit event name and the scorecard's 'call (confidence, grounding)' prefix so existing tools still parse it
Called Ollama directly instead of editing the frozen news-gate client, to add a fixed seed
Updated an existing test to patch the new call path, keeping its intent
Verified determinism by asking twice with the same facts
why: Gemma was judging bracket trades without seeing the bracket; the math was missing and the noise was in.
lesson: Before changing a record format, grep for every reader of it (memory.py, scorecard.py) and keep what they parse. Determinism (temperature 0 + seed) is a precondition for scoring a model.

task: Tie the Blackwell GPU into the research: factor library, quintile tests, blends, multiple-testing correction.
steps: Found the GPU stack in the Microsoft Store Python (torch 2.11 cu128 with sm_120, CuPy 13.6) and verified a real matmul on the device before relying on it
Kept the trading venv untouched: export panels from the project venv, compute in the GPU interpreter (same pattern as TradingAgents)
Validated the Romano-Wolf code on synthetic noise and on a planted signal before any real data
Committed the factor list, directions and pass rule before the first run
Read the wrong-way low-vol/MAX result as a data defect (survivorship), not a discovery
why: The operator wanted the GPU used; the most valuable use is making many tests cheap AND correcting for them in the same run.
lesson: A result that contradicts decades of evidence in both periods is first a question about the data. Speed is only safe when the multiple-testing correction runs in the same job.
